topic: The publish trigger uses tail_count_since_snapshot or tail_bytes_since_snapshot above
canonical_claim: The publish trigger uses `tail_count_since_snapshot` or `tail_bytes_since_snapshot` above configured thresholds and no longer requires entries to age; `snapshot_min_log_age_ms`, `TailLogEntry`, `tail_since_snapshot`, `snapshot_base_state`, and `CasRefLatePredecessorObserved` are removed.

topic: A late _log with id L satisfying sealed_from
canonical_claim: A late `_log` with id `L` satisfying `sealed_from < L <= newest_snapshot_id` is reported with a warning and one `RefLateLogDetected` event, never GET-revived, and left for ordinary covered-log cleanup.

topic: At an unclean mount, recovery LIST and replay
canonical_claim: At an unclean mount, recovery LIST and replay are followed by an immediate snapshot PUT seal before the mount opens writable.

topic: The recovery seal ID is RefTxnId(my_epoch - 1
canonical_claim: The recovery seal ID is `RefTxnId(my_epoch - 1, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)`, which covers every late log from every dead epoch below `my_epoch`.

topic: A lane refuses to allocate new IDs past
canonical_claim: A lane refuses to allocate new IDs past an unresolved PUT in release builds and uses `chassert` for the same wedge invariant in debug builds.

topic: A standalone committed-file removal without a directory drop
canonical_claim: A standalone committed-file removal without a directory drop publishes one repoint containing the manifest without the removed entry.

topic: A repoint publishes the new manifest closure before
canonical_claim: A repoint publishes the new manifest closure before backend observation and atomically moves ownership onto the same ref key; the old manifest is reclaimed by normal GC.

topic: The repoint primitive serializes concurrent repoints through the
canonical_claim: The repoint primitive serializes concurrent repoints through the per-table single-writer ref lane and promote CAS.

topic: After the mutable-file deletion sweep, resolved refs contain
canonical_claim: After the mutable-file deletion sweep, resolved refs contain `manifest_id`, `manifest_size`, and `published_at_ms`, while the access API is `publishEntries(dst, entries, op, allow_repoint)` and no production code retains mutable-file fields or predicates.

topic: The CAS refsnaplog migration covers cas_ref_log objects at
canonical_claim: The CAS refsnaplog migration covers `cas_ref_log` objects at `_log/<txn_id>` and `cas_ref_snap` objects at `_snap/<snapshot_id>`, moving both from binary codecs to the phase-1 text file shape.

topic: A cas_ref_log object represents exactly one committed RefLogTxn
canonical_claim: A `cas_ref_log` object represents exactly one committed `RefLogTxn`, containing one namespace, one transaction ID, and that transaction's vector of `RefOp` entries.

topic: The recovery seal is an ordinary RefTableSnapshot published
canonical_claim: The recovery seal is an ordinary `RefTableSnapshot` published at synthetic `snapshot_id = {my_epoch-1, UINT64_MAX}` with `sealed_from` set to the greatest applied reference transaction ID.

topic: sealed_from is an optional RefTxnId whose absence and
canonical_claim: `sealed_from` is an optional `RefTxnId` whose absence and presence must remain distinguishable in the snapshot wire format; it is not represented by a sentinel value.

topic: Every RefTxnId field in refsnaplog text, including the
canonical_claim: Every `RefTxnId` field in refsnaplog text, including the synthetic seal sequence `UINT64_MAX`, is serialized as a decimal string rather than a JSON number.

topic: cas_part_manifest becomes a PayloadHybrid object consisting of a
canonical_claim: `cas_part_manifest` becomes a `PayloadHybrid` object consisting of a header line, descriptor meta line, sorted JSON entry records, a {"n":count} trailer, and a raw payload zone for inline bytes.

topic: Blob manifest entries carry ha, h, and sz
canonical_claim: Blob manifest entries carry `ha`, `h`, and `sz`; inline entries carry `il` and no blob reference; entry records are sorted by canonical path without duplicates.

topic: A failed repoint of an existing ref must
canonical_claim: A failed repoint of an existing ref must not drop that ref during compensation: `publishStaging` returns false for the repoint path, so the ref is absent from `created_refs` and is not rolled back as newly created.

topic: After cas_ref_snap switched to zstd-framed text, appending garbage
canonical_claim: After `cas_ref_snap` switched to zstd-framed text, appending garbage to a zstd frame causes one-shot decompression to fail with `Src size is incorrect`.

topic: The corrected seal-conflict test constructs a valid foreign
canonical_claim: The corrected seal-conflict test constructs a valid foreign seal with the same namespace and seal id `(2, MAX)`, `sealed_from = (2,1)`, and three committed rows, then proves adoption with `listRefs().size() == 3`.

topic: The plan's Atomic-layout route() contract folds moving/<part>/<file> into
canonical_claim: The plan's Atomic-layout `route()` contract folds `moving/<part>/<file>` into the live table namespace with ref `<part>` and file `<file>`, while a bare `<table>/moving` container has an empty ref and file.

topic: The planned RefCowMap API is a read-only-iterator, std::map<String
canonical_claim: The planned `RefCowMap` API is a read-only-iterator, `std::map<String, RefCommittedRow>`-compatible subset covering keyed lookup, ordered iteration, size/empty, emplace, insert-or-assign, erase, equality, and materialization.

topic: Changing RefTableState::committed to RefCowMap leaves keyed-read and ordered-iteration
canonical_claim: Changing `RefTableState::committed` to `RefCowMap` leaves keyed-read and ordered-iteration consumers compatible; `CasRefProtocol.cpp::applySetPayload` is the exceptional site that must be rewritten for read-only iterators.

topic: RefCowMap preserves canonical snapshot ordering by bytewise ref_name
canonical_claim: `RefCowMap` preserves canonical snapshot ordering by bytewise `ref_name`, so the codec boundary remains `std::vector<RefCommittedRow>` and snapshot bytes remain unchanged.

topic: CasRefLedger::flushRefBatch must call rt->state.committed.materialize() immediately after
canonical_claim: `CasRefLedger::flushRefBatch` must call `rt->state.committed.materialize()` immediately after installing `final_txn` under the existing `state_mutex`, so later trial copies stay proportional to the current flush.

topic: Hot ref-table paths are keyed lookups, while snapshotOf
canonical_claim: Hot ref-table paths are keyed lookups, while `snapshotOf`, `listRefs`, and `dropNamespace` are the cold paths that require full scans.

topic: Ordered iteration is load-bearing because snapshotOf and removal-transaction
canonical_claim: Ordered iteration is load-bearing because `snapshotOf` and removal-transaction construction require bytewise-sorted iteration by `ref_name`; an unordered overlay is insufficient.

topic: The ordered-identifier and snapshot negative tests treat source-edge
canonical_claim: The ordered-identifier and snapshot negative tests treat source-edge ID zero, out-of-order source-edge records, zero `RefTxnId` components, and `sealed_from` greater than `snapshot_id` as invalid states.

topic: OwnerObject gains std::optional<uint64_t> retired_at_ms, serialized under the key
canonical_claim: `OwnerObject` gains `std::optional<uint64_t> retired_at_ms`, serialized under the key `"rt"`; the field is absent for an owner that has never been retired.

topic: The two budget-relevant ref-ledger encodings are pure sums
canonical_claim: The two budget-relevant ref-ledger encodings are pure sums of independent per-row or per-op byte contributions plus O(1) framing: snapshot rows depend only on their own fields, and hypothetical removal operations depend only on owner kind, ref name, and manifest reference.

topic: The counters are pure functions of (committed, precommits)
canonical_claim: The counters are pure functions of `(committed, precommits)`, so copying a `RefTableState` carries consistent totals without additional synchronization or scans.; For the incremental ref-ledger byte counters, `RefTableState` equality/hashing in tests is safe only because the counters are a pure function of the rows (any two states with equal rows have equal counters); the residual risk to verify is that no test constructs a `RefTableState` with populated rows outside the two designated seeding paths.
